problem: Traditional last-mile delivery navigation relies on expensive high-precision maps, while learning-based semantic navigation methods generalize poorly to diverse real-world outdoor environments; existing benchmarks also do not reflect residential last-mile delivery challenges.
motivation: Autonomous delivery robots need scalable, low-cost navigation that works without GPS, pre-mapping or real-time map updates. Off-the-shelf OpenStreetMap is readily available, and foundation models (LLMs/VLMs) can interpret instructions and localize, so combining them with classic navigation can give a lightweight solution.
key_idea: Combine OpenStreetMap with LLM instruction parsing, VLM-based GPS-free global localization and local waypoint replanning on top of classic navigation algorithms for open-air last-mile delivery.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract suggests that pairing foundation-model semantics (instruction understanding, localization) with classical planning, plus local replanning to correct OSM inaccuracies and environment changes, is what gives robustness without high-precision maps.
method: LLM instruction interpretation: parses delivery instructions into navigation goals/targets.
OSM-based map representation: uses off-the-shelf OpenStreetMap as a lightweight global map, avoiding pre-mapping.
VLM global localization: localizes the robot without GPS, without real-time map updates and without entrance recognition.
Local replanning: dynamically adjusts waypoints in response to environmental changes and OSM inaccuracies.
Classic navigation stack: foundation-model outputs are combined with classical navigation algorithms for execution.
New residential navigation benchmark: designed for last-mile delivery, released with code.
